Subject: Token capacity runbook & throughput session — scheduling

Hi Samir / Acme ops team —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The next step we discussed was a focused session to align on peak token throughput targets and run the capacity runbook against a short staging run so you can validate latency and p95 behavior under expected peaks. Goal: leave the meeting with a clear test window and ownership for the run.

Proposed agenda (30–45m):
- Quick alignment on traffic shape / max concurrent requests (5m)
- Target token/sec and token/session objectives (5m)
- Runbook walk-through (10m)
- Test scheduling: envs, credentials, and timeline (10m)
- Action items & owners (5m)

Availability from our side: Thu 10/22 09:00–11:00 PT, Fri 10/23 13:00–16:00 PT. If neither works, list a couple of preferred slots and we’ll flex. Attendees: me, Marcus (serving/runtime), Karthik (perf engineering). I’m attaching a first-pass runbook and a throughput matrix for you to scan before the meeting.

Attachments: token-capacity-runbook-v1.pdf; throughput-matrix.xlsx

Thanks —
Kimberly
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear agenda and the materials. Thu 10/22 09:00 PT would work for most of the ops team; we have a delivery window that afternoon. Two quick clarifications before we lock in: 
1) For the staging run, do you need access to our staging VPC or is the test purely client-driven against your hosted endpoints?
2) Can you confirm the test harness you recommend — we typically use a homegrown loader but can run your jmeter scripts if that’s preferable.

I’ll loop in our SRE lead (copied to ops+acme) if we need VPC creds.

Samir

Hi Samir —

Short answers: we can run client-driven tests against our hosted endpoints and provide a short harness (JMeter + Python wrapper) that mirrors your traffic shape. If you want us inside your staging VPC for end-to-end ingress/e2e latency, we’ll need a short IAM role and an ephemeral subnet route — that’s doable but takes a little ops coordination.

For the meeting: let’s plan to spend 10m on environment matrix so we’re explicit about which tests require VPC access vs. client-only. I attached a sample jmeter pack we use for tokenized throughput. If you prefer, we can run the initial 15-minute smoke during the call and then schedule a longer 2-hour window for the full run.

Attachments: jmeter-acme-scripts.zip

Thanks,
Marcus
